name: Ireland
headline: Ireland: +8.0% growth in 2025, 2.1% inflation, debt 35% of GDP
sections: Ireland is a $680 billion economy (2025), the world's 25th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +8.0% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $155K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 33.9% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 2.1% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.1% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.7% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 10.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 35% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 57% in 2020. The general government balance is +1.9% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +8.0% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 240% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 10.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 24% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 83.0 years (2024). Population: 5.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
